latest_release.name: v12.0.0
latest_release.body:
Both templates now share one version number and ship together.

| Package | Previous | New |
|---|---|---|
| [Ardalis.CleanArchitecture.Template](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Ardalis.CleanArchitecture.Template/) (`clean-arch`) | 11.1.1 | **12.0.0** |
| [Ardalis.MinimalClean.Template](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Ardalis.MinimalClean.Template/) (`min-clean`) | 1.1.1 | **12.0.0** |

```bash
dotnet new install Ardalis.CleanArchitecture.Template
dotnet new install Ardalis.MinimalClean.Template
```

Upgrading an existing project? See the [v11 → v12 migration guide](https://cleanarchitecture.ardalis.com/migration-guides/v11-to-v12/).

## Highlights

- **.NET 11.** All solutions target `net11.0`, and every package is on its latest stable version, including FastEndpoints 9 and xUnit v3.
- **`Get` use case renamed to `GetById`** (`GetContributorByIdQuery` and `GetContributorByIdHandler`), matching the `GetById` endpoint (#1202).
- **NsDepCop rules in MinimalClean** enforce the boundaries between feature slices at build time (#1203, #1204).

## Fixes

- `ContributorId` validation no longer rejects EF Core temporary keys, which made inserts fail (#1195).
- The `UseDbGeneratedIds` migration no longer fails on SQL Server (#1194).
- Project names that aren't valid namespaces, such as names with hyphens, now produce correctly renamed files (#484).
- Functional tests fall back to SQLite when Docker is unavailable or can't run Linux containers (#1073, #1189).

## Cleaner generated solutions

- `clean-arch` solutions now include a `.gitignore`.
- `clean-arch` solutions no longer contain a stray copy of MinimalClean, and installing the package no longer registers `min-clean`.
- Files that only belong in this repository are no longer copied into new solutions: `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `icon.png`, `.claude/`, and two outdated testing notes.

## Docs

The docs moved to **[cleanarchitecture.ardalis.com](https://cleanarchitecture.ardalis.com/)** (#1205). They have new pages on [Testing](https://cleanarchitecture.ardalis.com/testing/), [Enforcing Dependency Rules](https://cleanarchitecture.ardalis.com/dependency-rules/), and [Unit of Work and Transactions](https://cleanarchitecture.ardalis.com/unit-of-work-and-transactions/).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/ardalis/CleanArchitecture/compare/v11.1.1...v12.0.0

[![Follow @nimblepros](https://img.shields.io/twitter/follow/nimblepros?label=Follow%20%40nimblepros)](https://twitter.com/intent/follow?screen_name=nimblepros)

`dotnet new` templates for building ASP.NET Core applications with [Clean Architecture](https://8thlight.com/blog/uncle-bob/2012/08/13/the-clean-architecture.html), also known as hexagonal, ports-and-adapters, or onion architecture. The domain model sits at the center, and dependencies point inward toward it.

There are two templates:

- **Full Clean Architecture (`clean-arch`)**: a multi-project solution (Core, UseCases, Infrastructure, Web) with DDD patterns, CQRS via Mediator, and FastEndpoints. Best for larger, long-lived applications.
- **Minimal Clean Architecture (`min-clean`)**: a single project organized by vertical slices, with layer boundaries enforced by [NsDepCop](https://github.com/realvizu/NsDepCop). Best for MVPs and smaller applications.

A complete sample application lives in [`/sample`](https://github.com/ardalis/CleanArchitecture/tree/main/sample).

## Getting Started

Install the templates from NuGet:

```powershell
dotnet new install Ardalis.CleanArchitecture.Template
dotnet new install Ardalis.MinimalClean.Template
```

Create a solution from either template:

```powershell
# Full Clean Architecture
dotnet new clean-arch -o Your.ProjectName

# Minimal Clean Architecture
dotnet new min-clean -o Your.ProjectName
```

## Documentation

**Everything else is in the docs: [cleanarchitecture.ardalis.com](https://cleanarchitecture.ardalis.com/).** That includes getting started, choosing between the templates, design decisions, dependency rules, and [migration guides](https://cleanarchitecture.ardalis.com/migration-guides/) for upgrading from earlier versions.
